title: Rotating Rubik's Cube
blurb: A classic Rubik's cube in vivid primary colors spinning smoothly in 3D.
technique:
The cube is a single `div` with `transform-style: preserve-3d` nested inside a `perspective: 700px` scene container. This pair — the perspective parent and the preserve-3d child — is the minimum required to place any number of child elements into the same shared 3D space without flattening them back to 2D.

Six face `div`s are absolutely positioned inside the cube, each filling the full 240×240px footprint. They are placed into their correct positions with a two-step CSS transform: first a `rotateX` or `rotateY` to orient the face (e.g. `rotateY(90deg)` for the right face), then `translateZ(120px)` to push it out by exactly half the cube's depth. Each face uses a CSS `grid` (3×3, `repeat(3, 1fr)`) with a black `#111` background and 7px gaps — the gaps and the 10px face padding form the visible frame and dividers that read as a real Rubik's cube. Each cell is a `.sticker` div with `border-radius: 4px` and a classic color: red, orange, blue, green, white, or yellow.

Continuous rotation is driven entirely by CSS: a `@keyframes spin` animation sweeps `rotateY` from 0° to 360° over 10 seconds with `linear` timing and `infinite` repeat. A fixed `rotateX(-28deg)` is baked into both keyframe states so the top face remains in view throughout the full spin, ensuring three faces are always visible simultaneously.

The ground shadow is a plain 2D `div` — a blurred `radial-gradient` ellipse positioned below the scene in normal document flow. Keeping it outside the 3D context means it never distorts with the cube's perspective; `filter: blur(6px)` softens the edge to mimic a diffuse area shadow and give the cube visual weight.
